recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If Permission is reviewed in the Data Access Policies IG, preserve the existing exclusion of Person there; no FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-34884.
issue_request: FHIR-34884 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for the Security work group. It requested removing Person from Permission.asserter because Person is for shared demographics rather than actors, and the approved target list used Patient, Practitioner, RelatedPerson, PractitionerRole, Organization, and CareTeam.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-34884. Commit 2c7d674ebe5bfdd04b2239cbb6d5990931b20aad changed source/permission/structuredefinition-Permission.xml on 2022-02-28 from Reference(Person) to a multi-target Reference that excluded Person and added Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, CareTeam, Patient, Device, and RelatedPerson. Later Permission source kept Person absent.
additional_context: Later security changes added HealthcareService and other agent-reference adjustments under FHIR-49672/FHIR-49304, and FHIR-51482 removed a duplicate Group target, without reintroducing Person. Commit 0e2a8a7f839d5e1a43787523daccf07d958362f3 removed Permission from the current core build and changed core Security and Privacy narrative links to the HL7 Data Access Policies IG. A bounded check of HL7/data-access-policies shows current Permission.asserter also lacks Person.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No core source change is needed because the seed issue's substantive change was already applied and the current core checkout no longer owns a Permission.asserter definition.

related_jiras.note: Applied later Security issue adding HealthcareService as a recognized agent target for Permission without reintroducing Person.
Resolved-change-required workflow actor guidance says Person cannot ever be a participant and informed later agent-target context, but it is not a separate decided issue in this run.
